problem: Existing open-vocabulary grounding either couples object search with costly online exploration, or does static one-shot retrieval/reranking over a pre-built scene graph or map. These fail on same-category instance ambiguity, relational (support-object) queries, and make loop-control decisions implicit.
motivation: Objects anchor perception, reasoning and action in navigation, manipulation and embodied QA, and evidence is often already captured in RGB-D streams. Grounding should therefore decide what evidence to inspect next, compare candidates and decide when to stop, rather than return the top retrieved object.
key_idea: Treat object grounding as a typed closed loop (plan -> detect -> selection plan -> select -> judge) in which an LLM/VLM judge chooses accept/continue/abort and passes structured hints to the next loop, wrapped by a light outer harness for task context.
insight: Feedback between loops is what makes iteration useful: 'No Feedback' (63.42 avg S@1) is no better than 'Single-shot' (63.55), while the full method reaches 67.29. Replacing the VLM selector with a rule selector causes the largest drop (61.03), so candidate-level visual verification matters most; support targets and a structured selection planner help as well. Planner capability dominates API-family sensitivity.
method: Typed loop state: FinderRequest, SearchPlan, LoopContext and LoopState objects keep the protocol stable and retries inspectable, so modules can be swapped locally.

Query-conditioned planning: an LLM planner outputs a primary target, optional support targets (with execution modes global/local_after_primary/conditional/none), 2+2 detection phrases, and a ScopePlan (room/floor priors, frame budgets, global reserve, explored constraints).

Scoped frame routing and detection: the router samples posed frames under the scope budget (cap 200 frames, stride 10); phrase-conditioned SAM3 masks are backprojected to 3D, clustered and deduplicated into candidates.

Candidate-centric evidence: one evidence card per primary candidate (representative views, geometry, support relations); a typed selection planner shortlists candidates and picks views, and a VLM selector gives factual image-grounded matches only.

Loop judge and cross-loop feedback: the judge combines visual facts, support-relation metrics, room-binding facts and history to accept/continue/abort, and emits next-loop hints (follow-up candidates, explored regions, phrase retargeting vs routing changes); max 3 loops.
Outer harness: injects step labels, resolved-object history, future-step context, mentioned entities or room hints into the request interface without modifying the inner loop.

setting.backbone: MiMo-v2-Pro planner/judge + Qwen 397B-A17B VLM (frozen APIs), SAM3 detector
setting.model_size: Qwen 397B-A17B (10B-class to 17B active); MiMo-v2-Pro size not stated
setting.action_space: no motion; outputs a 3D object location and accept/continue/abort loop actions
setting.simulator: Habitat/HM3D (offline RGB-D streams) plus real-world RGB-D captures
setting.privileged: known camera poses; optional room/floor priors for simple queries; pre-captured full RGB-D coverage of the scene

numbers.extra: 3 loops, 200 frame cap; simple queries use room priors

results: On the authors' Object Retrieval benchmark, Finder gets 66.24 average S@1 versus 50.49 for HOV-SG (+15.75) and 59.93 S@0.5 versus 36.83 for DualMap. It also beats DAAAM+GPT on SG3D (s-acc 25.91 vs 22.16) and has the best PosErr and TempErr on OC-NaVQA, but its QA accuracy (0.540) is below DAAAM (0.711).
limitations: Assumes pre-captured RGB-D streams with known poses; there is no active exploration or online scene update.
Cannot aggregate over multiple objects (e.g. counting), which hurts QA accuracy; per-query runtime is high (about 80-96 s).
Main benchmark is self-built and small on the real-world side (82 queries, hard only); baselines were re-run by the authors, and results depend on API models and the planner.
